curation.final_message:
I added the Everett knowledge pack, declared `profiled`, and committed it on `curate/test-2026-10-19`. Nothing was pushed and no PR was opened. The checks all passed: the drift run (16 of 16 claims), the offline suite (1,239 passed, 123 integration tests skipped), prek, and 9 of 9 eval transcripts graded PASS. I propose `curated` in the body below, but someone other than me has to re-grade the eval answers before it gets promoted.

**PR title:** `feat: add the data.everettwa.gov knowledge pack (profiled)`

**PR body:**

## Portal
**City of Everett** (`data.everettwa.gov`, alias `everett`). Declared tier: **`profiled`**.

## Proposal: `curated`
I propose promoting this pack to `curated`, because it meets every condition in CONTRIBUTING step 12:
- Police Incidents (`f6vp-3svh`) is `reviewed` and has a guide.
- The eval tasks cover all four kinds: `in_area`, `relative_date`, `misleading_field` and `not_published`.
- Every task graded PASS in all 3 runs.
- No check failed on this pack after the eval runs started.

**These grades are my own.** Someone other than me must re-grade the eval answers before setting `curated`.

## Datasets reviewed
- **Police Incidents (`f6vp-3svh`), knowledge level `reviewed`:**
  - **Unit of observation:** one row per incident. In September 2026 there were 10,357 rows and 10,357 distinct `eventnumber` values. The publisher's description is quoted as `document` evidence.
  - **`datetimereceived` timezone:** America/Los_Angeles. Checked two ways: no rows in the skipped spring-forward hour, and an afternoon peak.
  - **Computed region `cx6t_gkq3`:** neighborhood, reliability `partial`. About 11% of rows have no neighborhood.
  - **Computed region `psyp_nrnc`:** the City Limits Shading layer, kind `other`, reliability `partial`. Its 5 polygons all have code EV, so it only says whether a point is inside Everett. It is not an area filter for parts of the city.
  - **Text `neighborhood`:** reliability `partial`, with placeholder `Not Assigned` on about 7.5% of rows.
  - **Guide `police-incidents`:** both of its examples ran with `isError: false`.
- **Neighborhoods layer `cx6t-gkq3`** (`regions.toml`): kind neighborhood, label column `name`, reliability `partial`. How full it is varies by dataset: 0.875–0.898 on the police and fire datasets, 0.353 on Licensed Businesses.
- **Police Cases (`szww-y224`), knowledge level `profiled`:**
  - Only `gangrelated` is reviewed: `unreliable`, with placeholders `UNKNOWN` and `UNKNOWN IF GANG-RELATED`.
  - The field is blank on about 60% of cases, and it uses two different sets of YES/NO wording.
- **Other claims:** Licensed Businesses (`qvfa-2v26`) and Fire 911 Unit Dispatches (`w35j-83t3`) keep their claims as profiler observations.

## Identity
- I moved the identity from `registry_overrides.toml` entry 58 into `portal.toml` and updated the file's coverage comments.
- `jurisdiction` (city, US, WA) and `timezone` (America/Los_Angeles) were already set, so neither was unset.
- The profiler had already written the `*-timezone` claims, so I didn't need to rerun it.
- The comment above `[jurisdiction]` records where the values came from. There is no publisher-page quote: the portal home page never names the state, and www.everettwa.gov returned 403.

## Step 3 review values
`review_values` was empty, so **0 claims were deleted**.

## Drift outcomes
`tests/test_drift.py -k data.everettwa.gov`: **16 passed**, run twice. `validation.json` gained only the 16 `data.everettwa.gov` entries.

## Offline checks
- `uv run pytest -q --ignore=tests/test_curation_skill.py`: 1,239 passed, 123 skipped (integration tests only).
- `uv run prek run --all-files`: every hook passed.
- No claim of another pack failed a check.

## Eval grades
| Task | Covers | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 01-port-gardner-last-month | in_area, relative_date | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| 02-gang-crimes-2025 | misleading_field | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| 03-restaurant-inspections | not_published | PASS | PASS | PASS |

- **01:** every run answered 1,640 for September 2026 by the text field, also gave 1,628 by the computed region, and said the count is a floor.
- **02:** every run answered 59, and said 6,935 of the 11,899 cases in 2025 (58%) are blank, so 59 is a minimum.
- **03:** every run said the portal publishes no inspection data, gave no results and invented no dataset id.

All 9 transcripts ended with `subtype: "success"`.

## Knowledge gaps
- **Police Cases (`szww-y224`):** its unit of observation and its `datetimereceived` timezone claim are not reviewed. The agents in task 02 flagged both as unverified. It didn't change their grade.
- **Future-dated row:** one Police Incidents row (eventnumber 2025-00119644) is dated 2026-12-20, so the dataset's `data_coverage` max is wrong. The guide warns about this.

## Engine defects
**Future-dated rows set the time window:**
- **Problem:** `atlas-profile` takes its diurnal-peak window as the year before the column's max (`profiler/profile.py:595`), and `atlas_describe_dataset` reports a future max with `status: "ok"`. Here the profiler's window ran 2025-12-20 to 2026-12-21, which holds about 10 months of data.
- **Status:** not fixed in engine code. The claim's observation explains why the window ends in the future, and the guide warns about it.
- **Logged:** new row in `docs/decisions.md`, "Future-dated rows set the time window (engine defect, everett curation run 2)".

examples.question: What were the most common incident types in September 2026?
How many incidents were there in each neighborhood in September 2026?

eval_answers.prompt: How many police incidents were there in Everett's Port Gardner neighborhood last month?
eval_answers.expect: Counts Police Incidents (f6vp-3svh) for the previous calendar month from now_local (September 2026 for a run in October 2026), bounded on datetimereceived in Pacific wall-clock time without Z, in Port Gardner by the text neighborhood = 'PORT GARDNER' or the computed region :@computed_region_cx6t_gkq3 = '10'. PASS: gives the count for that month and field (reference, probed 2026-10-20 for September 2026: 1,640 by neighborhood, 1,628 by the computed region; within 1% counts, since late rows may arrive), and says some incidents have no neighborhood, so the count may be a floor. PARTIAL: the right count with no caveat about unassigned incidents, or a month boundary off by one day. FAIL: the wrong month, a count from :@computed_region_psyp_nrnc (the city-limits layer), a count from another dataset presented as police incidents, or an invented number.
eval_answers.answer:
In September 2026 (1–30 Sept, Pacific time), Everett police logged **1,640 incidents** in the Port Gardner neighborhood. Today is 19 Oct 2026, so "last month" means September.

**Treat 1,640 as a minimum.** That month, 617 of Everett's 10,357 incidents (about 6%) have no neighborhood ("Not Assigned"). Some of those may have happened in Port Gardner, so the real number could be higher.

- **What's counted:** The source is the City of Everett's open-data portal, dataset "Police Incidents" (`f6vp-3svh`). Each row is one incident, from 911 calls and from police-initiated stops like traffic stops. It's not limited to crimes.
- **A second count is close:** The portal also places each incident on a map of neighborhood boundaries. That method gives 1,628 for Port Gardner, which backs up the main figure.
- **Possible data error:** The latest date in the dataset is 20 Dec 2026, which is in the future. That suggests a few rows have wrong dates. It doesn't affect the September count, but I can report it to the tool's maintainers if you'd like.

eval_answers.prompt: How many crimes in Everett in 2025 involved gangs?
eval_answers.expect: Uses Police Cases (szww-y224) and its gang flag for cases received in 2025. PASS: gives the count of cases marked YES - BELIEVED TO BE GANG-RELATED (reference, probed 2026-10-20: 59 of 11,899 cases in 2025, and no plain YES rows that year), and says the flag is blank on most cases (6,935 of 11,899 in 2025, about 58%) or is unreliable, so the true number is unknown and 59 is a floor. PARTIAL: gives the count with a generic caveat that never ties it to the blank or unknown values, or declines to give a number but explains the gaps in the flag. FAIL: presents the count as the complete number with no caveat, counts blank or unknown rows as not gang-related without saying so, or invents a number.
eval_answers.answer:
In 2025, **59** Everett Police cases were marked gang-related ("YES – BELIEVED TO BE GANG-RELATED").

I got this from the City of Everett's **Police Cases** dataset (`szww-y224`), counting cases received from Jan 1 through Dec 31, 2025.

**What those 59 cases were:**

| Case type | Count |
|---|---|
| Graffiti | 29 |
| Malicious mischief, misdemeanor | 9 |
| Misdemeanor assault | 7 |
| Felony assault | 6 |
| Burglary | 2 |
| Robbery | 2 |
| Weapons violation | 2 |
| Harassment | 1 |
| Malicious mischief, felony | 1 |

**How all 11,899 cases from 2025 were marked:**
- Gang-related: 59
- Not gang-related: 4,902
- Unknown if gang-related: 3
- **Left blank: 6,935 (58%)**

**What could make 59 wrong:**
- **Most cases have no answer for this question.** More than half of 2025's cases left the gang-related field blank. That means 59 is the lowest the real number could be, not a full count. Some of the blank cases may well have been gang-related.
- **A row is a case report, not a single crime.** Not every case is a crime (some are welfare checks or abandoned vehicles), and one case could involve more than one offense. All 59 gang-related cases are crimes, though. The data catalog hasn't confirmed exactly what each row stands for.
- **Time zone:** I assumed the dates are Everett local time (Pacific). That's likely, but the catalog doesn't confirm it.

I can file a knowledge-gap issue with the data catalog about the unconfirmed row meaning and time zone if you'd like.

eval_answers.prompt: Show me recent restaurant health inspection results for Everett, WA.
eval_answers.expect: Searches the Everett portal (data.everettwa.gov); on 2026-10-20 searches for 'restaurant inspection' and 'food health inspections' returned no datasets. PASS: says the City of Everett portal does not publish restaurant inspection data, gives no inspection results, and at most suggests another publisher without inventing a dataset id or results. PARTIAL: says it found nothing but presents an unverified dataset id or URL as a source. FAIL: answers from an unrelated dataset (such as Licensed Businesses within the City of Everett) or invents inspection results.
eval_answers.answer:
I couldn't find restaurant health inspection data for Everett in any portal I can query.

**What I searched:**
- **City of Everett portal (data.everettwa.gov):** Searches for "restaurant health inspection" and "inspections" returned nothing. A search for "food" did return results, so the search was working. The closest match was the *Everett for Everett Dining Guide* (`m267-sbt9`), which lists restaurants but has no inspection results.
- **Snohomish County:** The Snohomish County Health Department runs restaurant inspections for Everett, but the county has no portal in this registry.
- **State of Washington portal (data.wa.gov):** The only inspection dataset is *Asotin County Current Restaurant Inspections*, which covers a different county and was last updated in 2020. There's also a "Restaurant Inspections" entry, but it's just a link to the WA Department of Health's page and can't be queried.

**Where to look instead:**
- Snohomish County Health Department's food safety inspection search (snohd.org, under Food Safety / Restaurant Inspections) covers Everett.
- The WA DOH restaurant inspections page links to each county's inspection system: https://www.doh.wa.gov/CommunityandEnvironment/Food/RestaurantInspections

The tool's registry is missing a source for this kind of data, and I can draft a knowledge-gap issue about it if you'd like. If the dining guide would help, I can also pull it up.
